reply: nimum sits near P≈1.5–3. The 1/P coefficient is roughly constant over t, while the constant term grows with t. Full least-squares on a large time-basis reached about 2.6e-4, but with heavy collinearity, so it is not a readable law. I ran out of tool calls before I could pin down the time dependence.

import numpy as np
def equation(t, P, params):
    s=np.sqrt(t); l=np.log(t)
    return (params[0]+params[1]*t+params[2]*s)*P + (params[3]+params[4]*s+params[5]*l+params[6]*t)/P + params[7]*P**2 + params[8]*t + params[9]
